top_story.headline: The Existentialist Republic PAC tells the FEC its former treasurer repaid $7,438.74 he moved into an unauthorized account
top_story.dek: The committee says it recovered every dollar, refunded all contributors and has asked the FEC to approve its termination.
paragraphs: In a Form 99 received October 31, The Existentialist Republic PAC responds to FEC requests for additional information dated October 25, 2026, about its July Quarterly Report and its Termination Report. It says the three receipts on Schedule A, Line 17 of the July Quarterly Report are the repayment by former treasurer Clifford Michael Pickens of $7,438.74 in committee funds that he deposited into an unauthorized account, plus $61.26 reported as reimbursement of filing fees.

According to the filing, the committee reported the misappropriation to the FEC on a Form 99 on June 2, 2026 (FEC-1981008). Pickens repaid $3,500.00 on June 9 and $3,938.74 plus the $61.26 on June 15. The eight unauthorized disbursements are itemized to him on Schedule B, Line 29: $4,593.82 on the amended April Quarterly Report (FEC-2015104) and $2,844.92 on the July Quarterly Report (FEC-2015296). The amended April report carries the $4,593.82 as a debt owed to the committee on Schedule D, and the July report shows it repaid.

The committee says it has refunded all $8,648.00 in contributions through ActBlue, as reported on its Termination Report (FEC-2021762), and holds no cash and no debts. It says it has found no error on the July Quarterly Report or earlier reports that needs amending, and it asks the FEC to approve its termination. Christopher Armitage signed as treasurer. These are the committee's own statements, and the filing does not say whether any other agency has been told. The filing was received October 31, so there is no indexing lag.

sections.headline: One sitting senator's committee filed a Form 99
paragraphs: A single filing is tagged to a sitting lawmaker today, a loan forgiveness notice from the committee of Sen. Tommy Tuberville.

items: Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) forgave $10,158.63 in personal loan debt owed to him by Tuberville for Senate, Inc. The Form 99 says the forgiveness took effect October 14, 2026, and covers the remaining balance of a loan originally made June 27, 2019. The committee filed the notice October 31, signed by treasurer Randall E. Jones, with a letter from the senator dated October 14 attached. (Form 99)

sections.headline: Ten candidate Form 2 letters dominate a mostly routine batch of 15 RFAIs
paragraphs: All 15 letters are dated October 30, 2026, and carry a December 4 response deadline. Ten go to House and presidential candidates and concern basic errors on their FEC Form 2 statements of candidacy: a wrong or missing year of election, or a missing or non-compliant principal campaign committee name. The other five go to independent-expenditure PACs, a corporation filing electioneering notices and a multicandidate PAC. They cover late 24-hour and Form 9 reports, missing contributor itemization, missing support/oppose information and possible excessive contributions.

blocks.text: Candidates: year of election on Form 2 (candidate committees are not involved in these letters; the problems are on the candidates' own statements of candidacy)

items: FEC asks House candidate Tynesha Marie Rice (D-NY) to correct the year of election on her Form 2. The letter says the year provided appears to be incorrect and requests an amended Form 2. (RFAI)
FEC asks presidential candidate Derrick Michael Reid (Libertarian) to supply the year of election missing from his Form 2. The letter asks for an amended Form 2 that includes it. (RFAI)

FEC asks presidential candidate Shawniquea Kmoneytmt R Mayweather Jr. (independent) to correct the year of election on her Form 2. The letter's text is the same year-of-election item sent to Tynesha Marie Rice. (RFAI)
FEC asks presidential candidate Lois Willow Allen (Republican) to correct the year of election on her Form 2. The letter's text is the same year-of-election item sent to Tynesha Marie Rice. (RFAI)

blocks.text: Candidates: principal campaign committee name or address on Form 2

items: FEC asks presidential candidate Jared Charles Martin to provide the name and address of his principal campaign committee. The letter says neither was given on his Form 2 and asks for an amendment. (RFAI)

FEC asks presidential candidate Nicole Renee Rising (Republican) to rename her principal campaign committee to include her own name. Commission rules (11 CFR § 102.14(a)) require the committee name to include the name of the authorizing candidate. (RFAI)

FEC asks presidential candidate Scott Conroy Palmer (independent) to provide the name and address of his principal campaign committee. The letter's text is the same missing-committee item sent to Jared Charles Martin. (RFAI)

blocks.text: Candidates: both problems in one letter

items: FEC asks presidential candidate Cortay Johnson (Republican) to fix both the year of election and his committee's name on his Form 2. The letter says the year appears incorrect and that the principal campaign committee name does not include his name. (RFAI)

FEC asks presidential candidate Jeff Allen Tank Geddes Sr. to fix both the year of election and his committee's name on his Form 2. The two items match those sent to Cortay Johnson: an apparently incorrect election year and a committee name that omits the candidate's name. (RFAI)

FEC asks presidential candidate Daniel White (independent) to supply both the year of election and his principal campaign committee's name and address. The letter says neither was provided on his Form 2. (RFAI)

FEC asks the 32BJ United American Dream Fund to explain why its 24-hour independent expenditure reports appear to have been filed late. The July Quarterly letter also says the Form 5 shows independent expenditures on Line 7 and contributions on Line 6 but lacks the Schedule 5-A memo text identifying donors of more than $200 who gave to further independent expenditures. (RFAI)

FEC asks the Community Water Center Action Fund why its July Quarterly Form 5 reports independent expenditures but no contributions. Line 7 shows independent expenditure disbursements and Line 6 is blank, so the letter asks for Schedule 5-A itemization of donors above $200 or a clarification. (RFAI)

FEC asks Stand Up for Ohio (Ohio Organizing Campaign) to say whether its independent expenditures supported or opposed each federal candidate. The letter says its 48-hour report, received October 11, 2026, is missing that detail on Schedule 5-E. The letter's reference line gives the report period as 10/09/2026 to 11/03/2026. (RFAI)

FEC says USPB JV LLC filed a Form 9 electioneering notice late and left out the federal candidates it named. The agency asks the company to explain the untimely disclosure and to add the name, state, office and district of each candidate clearly identified. The letter says the Form 9 was received October 16, though its reference line says October 15. (RFAI)

FEC asks the Women's Political Committee Federal about contributions on its September Monthly report that appear to exceed the $5,000-per-election limit. The letter asks treasurer Stephen J. Kaufman to give the date and method of any refund or redesignation. (RFAI)

sections.headline: Two other Form 99s: one PAC's misappropriation response and a presidential committee's threshold statement
paragraphs: Besides the sitting senator's loan forgiveness, two Form 99s arrived October 31. The first, from The Existentialist Republic PAC, is the Top Story.

items: The Existentialist Republic PAC tells the FEC its former treasurer repaid $7,438.74 he deposited into an unauthorized account. The committee says it recovered the full amount, refunded $8,648.00 to contributors and asks to terminate. This was flagged for the keyword 'misappropriation', and the filing text describes the misappropriation the committee says it reported on June 2, 2026. (Form 99)

Fred Francis 2028, Inc. tells the FEC that it did not raise or spend more than $5,000 as of September 30, 2026. The one-sentence Form 99 comes from the Washington, D.C., committee of presidential candidate Fred Hagin Francis (Democrat). (Form 99)
11/3/2026 (2 days): General Election Day

blocks.text: Independent expenditures of $50K+ reported since 10/29/2026 (24/48-hour notices plus regular reports), counting only items not shown in an earlier edition. A shared vendor is a coordination-risk flag, not proof: FEC rules allow common vendors behind a firewall. Generic platforms (ActBlue, Google, postal, banks, broadcasters) are excluded.
